title: Negotiated schema adapter and incremental stream verification for constrained decoding
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This ticket implements a negotiated schema adapter plus an incremental stream verification layer to strengthen JSON mode enforcement and constrained decoding for streaming responses and tool/function-calling scenarios. The adapter will accept schema hints from the API contract and the model response, reconcile differences at token-granularity, and emit deterministic hook points for rollbacks or soft-fallbacks when the decoder drifts.

Motivation and context:
We've seen intermittent schema drift during partial-streaming (prefixes) where downstream parsers fail on final assembly because earlier tokens violated a narrow schema assumption. Existing tests focus on whole-output compliance; we need runtime, incremental checks that catch and remediate drift earlier to avoid API-level errors and poor UX in tool-calling flows. This ticket complements the batch-level schema suites by adding a streaming-first verification and negotiation mechanism.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: implement adapter logic in the serving runtime shim, instrument token-level verification hooks, add tests that emulate tool-calling interleaved with JSON tokens, and define soft-fallback policies (schema-hint negotiation and localized coercions).
- Out of scope: full end-to-end UI changes in Console (will add follow-up PM ticket), non-JSON schema languages (protobufs) and training model fine-tuning.

Design overview (high level):
1) Schema hint negotiation: when a request includes a schema (or one is inferred from the route), the runtime stores a compact descriptor. If the incoming token stream diverges, the adapter flags the earliest divergence and attempts a set of ordered mitigations: a) localized token correction heuristics (e.g., insert missing delimiters), b) request-level backoff to ask for schema-respecting regeneration, c) model variant failover.
2) Incremental verifier: a light-weight state machine runs during streaming to check partial AST conformance for common JSON constructs (arrays, objects, quoted strings, commas). The verifier returns stable checkpoints which the reassembly layer uses instead of naive concatenation.
3) Observer/metrics: expose metrics for "incremental-mismatch-count", "repair-applied", and latency impact of verification.

Deliverables:
- Runtime adapter code (C++/Rust shim) and public contract changes for the SDK to include schema hints.
- Integration test suite that simulates: (a) tool-calling interleaving tokens mid-structure, (b) partial-token drop scenarios, and (c) intentional drift cases to validate fallback ordering.
- Canary program plan and rollback criteria.

Rollout plan and safety:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable adapter for 5% of internal dev traffic and synthetic traffic for 1 week. Monitor metrics and error budgets.
- Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for selected customers with heavy tool-calling usage.
- Rollback: disable adapter or switch to "observe-only" mode if repair-applied rate > 0.5% and customer-facing errors increase.

Risks and mitigations:
- Increased token latency: mitigate by keeping verifier O(1) amortized per token and gating expensive heuristics behind sampling.
- Over-aggressive repairs causing semantic changes: repairs are conservative and logged; for high-sensitivity routes we default to request-level regeneration.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Negotiated+Schema+Adapter+Design
- Draft RFC: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/schem-adapter-draft
- Proto test vectors: github.com/redwood/infra/tests/stream-schema-vectors (WIP)
acceptance_criteria: Adapter successfully flags first-token divergence for >95% of synthetic drift cases
Repair heuristics are applied for documented classes and are reversible (logged)
No more than 0.2% increase in median per-token latency on canary traffic
Integration tests covering tool-calling interleaves pass in CI with deterministic outcomes
SDK accepts schema hints without breaking existing non-hinted routes
test_plan: Unit: state machine step-through for partial-object/array checkpoints
Integration: simulated tool-call interleave where tool output is injected mid-object
Chaos: drop tokens mid-stream and assert detector surfaces divergence and triggers fallback
Compatibility: run existing schema regression suites to prove no regressions
Performance: baseline token latency A/B test between adapter enabled/disabled
notes: Decision: prefer conservative localized corrections over aggressive re-gen for low-latency routes
Trade-off: more checks increase detection but also CPU cost; we will sample heavy routes initially
Follow-up: PM will create a Console exposable toggle for opt-in customers (separate ticket)
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Ticket created — initial scope and design sketch posted. Assigned to Diego for implementation plan.
2026-03-04 Diego Alvarez: Spike completed — prototype verifier implemented in runtime-shim. Found edge case with escaped quotes across token boundaries; added workaround in parser state machine.
2026-03-06 Priya Kapoor (PM): Reviewed design, asked for explicit canary criteria and customer communication plan. Added request to track repair-applied breakdown by route.
2026-03-09 Diego Alvarez: Integration tests added for tool-call interleave. Noted a regression in streaming telemetry (missing trace ids) — filed ENG-331002 to fix tracing.
2026-03-11 Design review (Liam O'Connor): UX note — Console should surface 'repair suggested' flags with example snippets. Will coordinate on follow-up ticket.

2026-03-12 Diego Alvarez: Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-15 to 5% internal dev traffic; dashboards wired to monitor incremental-mismatch-count and repair-applied ratios. PR draft: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4783
